title: Exact derived squares preserve specified composition identities
statement: Let C₀,C₁,C₂,D₀,D₁,D₂ be abelian categories with derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let Fᵢⱼ:Cᵢ→Cⱼ, Gᵢⱼ:Dᵢ→Dⱼ (ij=01,12,02) and Uᵢ:Cᵢ→Dᵢ be exact additive functors, with specified composition isomorphisms cF:F₀₂≅F₀₁⋙F₁₂ and cG:G₀₂≅G₀₁⋙G₁₂. Let qᵢⱼ:Uᵢ⋙Gᵢⱼ≅Fᵢⱼ⋙Uⱼ satisfy q₀₂(X);U₂(cF(X))=cG(U₀X);G₁₂(q₀₁(X));q₁₂(F₀₁X) for all X. Construct each derived q as inverse exact-composition comparison, derived ordinary q, and exact-composition comparison. Construct derived cF,cG by derived ordinary c followed by exact-composition comparison. Then precisely the same pasting identity holds at every bounded-below derived object K. The construction has the localization factorization recorded by mapDerivedCategoryPlusSquareIso_fac. There are no schemes, sections, cohomology, coefficient rings or inverse limits in this statement.

source.place: The localization universal property for exact functors; implemented by mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso_hom_app_factorsh and mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso_hom_app_factorsh in WeilConjectures/Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/ExactFunctor.lean.

proof.text: Expand the constructed square. Use the composition factorization for L and S to cancel the last composition comparison, then the natural-isomorphism factorization to replace the middle comparison by the localized termwise map. The composition factorization for R and G, precomposed with its inverse comparison, gives the remaining equality. All canceled arrows are specified isomorphisms; the argument does not assume nonzero categories or objects.

The remaining composition theorem: form both derived natural transformations and test on Qh of a bounded-below homotopy object. Postcompose with U₂ applied to the F₁₂ and F₀₁ factors, then the U₂ factor. On the left, the composition factorization for cF and naturality of the U₂ factor reduce to the square factorization for q₀₂. On the right, move the F₀₁ factor across q₁₂ by naturality, then apply the factorization for q₁₂ and q₀₁. Move the termwise q₀₁ across the G₁₂ factor; naturality of the cG comparison and its composition factorization yield the common U₀ and G₀₂ factors. What remains is Qh of the assumed ordinary equation, applied degreewise to a complex representative; it follows by functoriality and extensionality of complex maps. Cancel the three isomorphisms and use localization extensionality, then evaluate at K. Zero categories and zero objects require no exception.

lean.statement: theorem mapDerivedCategoryPlusSquareIso_comp (q₀₁ : U₀ ⋙ G₀₁ ≅ F₀₁ ⋙ U₁) (q₁₂ : U₁ ⋙ G₁₂ ≅ F₁₂ ⋙ U₂) (q₀₂ : U₀ ⋙ G₀₂ ≅ F₀₂ ⋙ U₂) (cF : F₀₂ ≅ F₀₁ ⋙ F₁₂) (cG : G₀₂ ≅ G₀₁ ⋙ G₁₂) (hq : ∀ X : C₀, q₀₂.hom.app X ≫ U₂.map (cF.hom.app X) = cG.hom.app (U₀.obj X) ≫ G₁₂.map (q₀₁.hom.app X) ≫ q₁₂.hom.app (F₀₁.obj X)) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus C₀) : (mapDerivedCategoryPlusSquareIso U₀ G₀₂ F₀₂ U₂ q₀₂).hom.app K ≫ U₂.mapDerivedCategoryPlus.map ((mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso cF ≪≫ mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso F₀₁ F₁₂).hom.app K) = (mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso cG ≪≫ mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso G₀₁ G₁₂).hom.app (U₀.mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj K) ≫ G₁₂.mapDerivedCategoryPlus.map ((mapDerivedCategoryPlusSquareIso U₀ G₀₁ F₀₁ U₁ q₀₁).hom.app K) ≫ (mapDerivedCategoryPlusSquareIso U₁ G₁₂ F₁₂ U₂ q₁₂).hom.app (F₀₁.mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj K)
